title: Good truncation reduces cohomological lower bounds to strict lower bounds
statement: For an abelian category A, a small filtered category I whose colimits in A exist and are exact, and an object K of D(A), suppose Hom from K in every integer shift commutes with canonical colimits of all I-diagrams of complexes sharing a termwise lower bound. Then for every I-diagram D with one common cohomological lower bound and every colimit cocone c with witness hc, K satisfies homColimitProperty for D composed with Q and Q(c). The comparison is the canonical map induced by c, not merely an abstract group isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12, common lower bound reduction in the proof of Lemma 6.3.14

proof.text: Choose the common lower bound a. Apply good truncation GE(a) to every stage. Each truncation projection is a quasi-isomorphism; the truncated complexes vanish strictly below a. Homology preserves the filtered colimits because those colimits in A are exact, so the induced colimit map of the truncation projections is also a quasi-isomorphism.

Compare the chosen cocone c with the canonical cocone of the truncated diagram. Its vertex map is the unique colimit isomorphism followed by the colimit of the truncation projections. The leg equality follows by the defining equations of colimit.desc and colimMap.

Apply Q, shifts and additive Hom from K. The stage and vertex maps are isomorphisms, compatible with the cocone legs. The assumed canonical strict-bounded comparison is invertible, so the supplied comparison is invertible as well, for every shift.
